'''Michael D. West''' (born 28 April 1953 in [[Niles, Michigan]]) is an American [[biogerontologist]]. His research focuses, on [[stem cell]]s,<ref>{{cite news |title= On Michael D. West and the Medical Crusade to Defeat Death
|url=http://blogs.tiu.edu/bioethics/2011/05/09/on-michael-d-west-and-the-crusade-to-defeat-death-part-1/ |work= Trinity International University blog|date= May 9, 2011}}</ref> [[cellular aging]] and [[telomerase]].<ref>{{cite news |title= A Blood Test Offers Clues to Longevity
|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2011/05/19/business/19life.html?pagewanted=all/ |work= New York Times|date= May 18, 2011}}</ref> He is the CEO of [[AgeX Therapeutics]].<ref>{{cite news |title= The Smart Money Is Piling Into Regenerative Medicine|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/patrickcox/2017/04/14/smart-money-is-piling-into-regenerative-medicine/#54bb1405b6c5 |work= Forbes.com |date= April 14, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title= AgeX Therapeutics lands $10 mln|url=https://www.pehub.com/2017/08/agex-therapeutics-lands-10-mln/ |work= PE HUB |date= August 17, 2017}}</ref> 

==Early life and education==
West was born in [[Niles, Michigan]]. He graduated from Niles Senior High School and received a [[Bachelor of Science|BS]] in psychology from the [[Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute]] in 1976. He then received a PhD in cell biology in 1989 from the [[Baylor College of Medicine]]. He did postdoctoral research at the [[University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center]]<ref>[https://embryo.asu.edu/pages/michael-d-west-1953 Michael D. West (1953- )]</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.michaelwest.org/MICHAEL_DAVID_WEST_CV_May_2021.pdf |title=MICHAEL DAVID WEST, B.S., M.S., Ph.D. |access-date=2022-11-25 |archive-date=2022-11-25 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221125124639/http://www.michaelwest.org/MICHAEL_DAVID_WEST_CV_May_2021.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref> at Dallas.

==Career==
West was founder, director, and chief scientific officer of [[Geron Corporation|Geron]], for which he secured [[venture capital]] investment from [[Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers]], [[Venrock]]<ref>{{cite web|title=SEC Schedule 13G, filed Feb. 17, 1999|url= http://yahoo.brand.edgar-online.com/DisplayFiling.aspx?TabIndex=2&FilingID=1363847&companyid=11441&ppu=%252fDefault.aspx%253fcompanyid%253d11441%2526amp%253bformtypeID%253d346}}</ref> and Domain Associates.<ref>{{cite web|title=Geron Corporation 10K 1996|url= http://www.bio.net/bionet/mm/ageing/1996-May/002331.html}}</ref> At Geron, West initiated and managed programs in telomere biology relating to aging, cancer and [[human embryonic stem cell]] technology.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bloomberg Longevity Economy Conference 2013 Panelist Bio |url=http://www.bloomberglink.com/people/michael-d-west-ph-d/ |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20130803060041/http://www.bloomberglink.com/people/michael-d-west-ph-d/ |archivedate=2013-08-03 }}</ref>

West was chairman of the board, chief scientific officer and CEO of [[Advanced Cell Technology]] (ACT), another biotechnology company focused on stem cell research. ACT later changed its name to Ocata Therapeutics, and was acquired by Japanese pharmaceutical company [[Astellas Pharma]] in February 2016.{{cn|date=April 2025}}

West was a CEO of BioTime, Inc. (NYSE: BTX), later renamed Lineage Cell Therapeutics (NYSE: LCTX). With them, he acquired the stem cell assets of Geron Corporation in a subsidiary of BioTime called Asterias Therapeutics (NYSE: AST), which was later merged with Lineage Cell Therapeutics. While at BioTime, he also founded and took public Oncocyte (NYSE: OCX), which was later renamed Insight Molecular Diagnostics, Inc. (NYSE: IMDX).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Oncocyte Changes Name to Insight Molecular Diagnostics Inc. (iMDx), Moves Headquarters to Nashville |url=https://investors.imdxinc.com/news-releases/2025/06-17-2025-120135632 |access-date=2026-03-11 |website=investors.imdxinc.com |language=en}}</ref>

West was CEO and founder of AgeX Therapeutics, acquired by Serina Therapeutics in 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1708599/000149315223030660/ex99-1.htm |access-date=2026-03-11 |website=www.sec.gov|title=Serina Therapeutics and AgeX Therapeutics Enter into Merger Agreement}}</ref>

West organized the first collaborative effort to isolate human [[pluripotent]] (embryonic) stem cells for the purpose of manufacturing products in regenerative medicine in collaboration with [[James Thomson (cell biologist)|James Thomson]] at the [[University of Wisconsin at Madison]], John Gearhart at [[Johns Hopkins School of Medicine]],<ref>{{cite journal |title= A decade of stem-cell research. An interview with John Gearhart, Director of the Institute for Regenerative Medicine at the University of Pennsylvania, USA|journal= EMBO Reports |date= December 12, 2008 |pmc=2613216 |pmid=19079128 |doi=10.1038/embor.2008.235 |volume=10 |pages=12–6 |author=Gearhart J|issue= 1 }}</ref> and Roger Pedersen at the [[University of California, San Francisco]].<ref>{{cite news |title= Stem-Cell Researcher Plans Move to U.K., Citing Unfriendly Political Climate in U.S.|url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB995232102935923565 |work= The Wall Street Journal |date= July 16, 2001}}</ref>

In their telomerase research, West and colleagues at Geron cloned the RNA component of telomerase<ref>{{cite journal | last=Feng | first=Junli | last2=Funk | first2=Walter D. | last3=Wang | first3=Sy-Shi | last4=Weinrich | first4=Scott L. | last5=Avilion | first5=Ariel A. | last6=Chiu | first6=Choy-Pik | last7=Adams | first7=Robert R. | last8=Chang | first8=Edwin | last9=Allsopp | first9=Richard C. | last10=Yu | first10=Jinghua | last11=Le | first11=Siyuan | last12=West | first12=Michael D. | last13=Harley | first13=Calvin B. | last14=Andrews | first14=William H. | last15=Greider | first15=Carol W. | last16=Villeponteau | first16=Bryant | title=The RNA Component of Human Telomerase | journal=Science | volume=269 | issue=5228 | date=1995 | issn=0036-8075 | pmid = 7544491 | doi=10.1126/science.7544491 | pages=1236–1241 | url=https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.7544491 | bibcode = 1995Sci...269.1236F | s2cid = 9440710| access-date=2025-08-05| url-access=subscription }}</ref> and collaborated with [[Thomas Cech]] (winner of 1989 Nobel Prize in Chemistry), with whom they cloned the catalytic component of the enzyme telomerase,<ref>{{cite news |title= Biotechnology Company Says It Has Cloned a Cancer Gene|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1997/08/18/business/biotechnology-company-says-it-has-cloned-a-cancer-gene.html |work= The New York Times |date= August 18, 1997}}</ref> and sponsored collaborative research in the laboratory of [[Carol Greider]], then at [[Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory]].<ref>Hall, Stephen (2003). "Merchants of Immortality: Chasing the New Dream of Life Extension". Houghton Mifflin. {{ISBN|0547561571}}. Page 320.</ref> Geron published evidence of the role of telomerase in cancer and cell immortalization in collaboration with Woodring Wright and Jerry Shay at the University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center at Dallas.<ref>{{cite journal | last=Kim | first=Nam W. | last2=Piatyszek | first2=Mieczyslaw A. | last3=Prowse | first3=Karen R. | last4=Harley | first4=Calvin B. | last5=West | first5=Michael D. | last6=Ho | first6=Peter L. C. | last7=Coviello | first7=Gina M. | last8=Wright | first8=Woodring E. | last9=Weinrich | first9=Scott L. | last10=Shay | first10=Jerry W. | title=Specific Association of Human Telomerase Activity with Immortal Cells and Cancer | journal=Science | volume=266 | issue=5193 | date=1994-12-23 | issn=0036-8075 | doi=10.1126/science.7605428 | pages=2011–2015 | url=https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.7605428 | bibcode = 1994Sci...266.2011K | s2cid = 11965342| access-date=2025-08-05| url-access=subscription }}</ref>

For the company's Scientific and Clinical Advisory Board, he recruited [[Günter Blobel]] (winner of the 1999 [[Nobel Prize]] in [[Physiology]]),<ref>Hall, Stephen (2003). "Merchants of Immortality: Chasing the New Dream of Life Extension". Houghton Mifflin. {{ISBN|0547561571}}. Page 151.</ref> [[Leonard Hayflick]], [[Carol Greider]] (winner of the 2009 Nobel Prize in Medicine), [[James Watson]] (winner of the 1962 Nobel Prize in medicine), and others.<ref>{{cite web|title=Geron Corporation 10K 1996|url= http://www.bio.net/bionet/mm/ageing/1996-May/002331.html}}</ref>

West has been a keynote speaker at events including World Stem Cell and is associated with 146 patents in the United States,<ref>{{cite web|title=Google Patent Search: West, Michael D|url=https://www.google.com/?tbm=pts#q=west+michael+d&safe=active&tbm=pts}}</ref> Australia, Japan, and elsewhere.<ref>{{cite web|title=Michael David West CV|url=http://michaelwest.org/Michael_West_CV.pdf|access-date=2013-09-15|archive-date=2014-07-26|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140726121115/http://www.michaelwest.org/Michael_West_CV.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref>{{better source needed|date=February 2018}}

West is a member of the [[Alcor Life Extension Foundation]]'s scientific advisory board.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.alcor.org/about/ |title=About Alcor: The World Leader in Cryonics |author=<!--Not stated--> |date= 14 November 2019|website=alcor.org |publisher= |access-date=May 14, 2023 |quote=}}</ref> He is a signatory of the Scientists’ Open Letter on [[Cryonics]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.biostasis.com/scientists-open-letter-on-cryonics/ |title=Scientists' Open Letter on Cryonics |author=<!--Not stated--> |date= |website=Biostasis |publisher= |access-date=May 14, 2023 |quote=}}</ref>

==Bibliography==
===Books===
West has authored and co-edited books on topics including animal cloning, aging, biogerontology, stem cells, stem cell biology, and regenerative medicine.

* 2002 ''Principles of Cloning'' {{ISBN|0-12-174597-X}}
* 2003 ''The Immortal Cell'', by Michael D. West, Doubleday {{ISBN|978-0-385-50928-2}}
* 2004 ''Handbook of Stem Cells: Volume 1 Embryonic Stem Cells'' {{ISBN|0-12-436642-2}}
* 2004 ''Handbook of Stem Cells: Volume 2 Adult and Fetal Stem Cells'' {{ISBN|0-12-436644-9}}
* 2006 ''Essentials of Stem Cell Biology'' {{ISBN|0-12-088442-9}}
* 2010 ''The Future of Aging'' {{ISBN|9048139988}}
* 2010 ''The Future of Aging: Pathways to Human Life Extension'' {{ISBN|978-90-481-3998-9}}
